title: NovAura Web OS: browser desktop, platform and Firebase backend
summary: The NovAura web edition: a full-screen desktop OS in the browser (windows, taskbar, launcher, many built-in apps), a landing page, a separate React + TypeScript platform app, and a Firebase backend (Cloud Functions v2 in TypeScript, Firestore and Storage rules). It was built as a one-stop shop and shelved for a ground-up rebuild, so treat it as a parts bin and a reference.
works: Everything builds: the web OS and landing page with Vite, the platform app with Vite, and the Firebase functions type-check with tsc (checked with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps --include=dev`, then each build).
The desktop shell runs in the browser: windows, taskbar, launcher and many built-in apps, the BuilderBot IDE and the kernel (IPC bus, subsystems).
The Firebase backend has real routes for auth, AI (many providers), generation, search, email (IMAP/SMTP), user and admin API keys, sync and assets.
unfinished: Several apps are shells or show sample data: the browser, terminal, git window and AI companion are partly built, creator earnings and royalties are mock data, and the Dojo world generator returns templates rather than worlds.
The Games Arena's HTML games (Nova Net Battler, Nova Strike, Gilded Cage) live in public/games/, which is not included, so the arena opens without them.
Payments are not finished: Stripe checkout redirects but no webhook confirms payment, orders have no download or license delivery, and domain buying is UI only.
Social feed and messages live in the browser (localStorage) with no backend sync, and signup has no email verification.
The secrets manager uses weak XOR obfuscation; do not store real keys in it as is.

Every key, admin email, staff gate code and staff token was removed. Set your own admin emails, gate code and keys before you deploy, and give functions/src/api/routes/drive.ts your own Google service account file (functions/src/service-account.json).
npm reports a React 19 peer conflict with the 3D packages, so install with --legacy-peer-deps.
notIncluded: Large media under public/ (about 390 MB): the HTML games, the Aetherium card art and the NovaHearts assets.
Environment files, Firebase project settings, exported user data and logs.
Experimental folders outside the build (synth_workspace, Aura-Nova-Genesis, dev-shell).
requirements: Your own Firebase project for the backend (Cloud Functions, Firestore, Storage, Hosting)
Your own API keys for any AI or payment provider you turn on
openWith: Run `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` then `npm run dev` in this folder for the web OS (it opens /os/). The platform app is in platform/ (its own install). The backend is in functions/: copy .env.example to .env, add your own keys, and deploy to your own Firebase project.
